claims.text: Accelerated coupled degradation during simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature is primarily driven by galvanic corrosion induced by the multiphase structure.
Multiphase structures induce galvanic corrosion effects.
Potential differences between constituent phases produce micro-galvanic cells.
The relevant multiphase microstructure includes an FCC phase and a sigma phase.
Galvanic coupling between the FCC and sigma phases accelerates corrosion.
Galvanic coupling between phases accelerates wear.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion will increase total degradation relative to a matched baseline.
The multiphase alloy will have a higher corrosion rate than a matched single-phase alloy or multiphase alloy lacking galvanic effects.
The multiphase alloy will have a higher wear rate than a matched single-phase alloy or multiphase alloy lacking galvanic effects.
The proposed mechanism applies over an elevated-temperature range of approximately 500–800 degrees Celsius.
A controlled comparison between multiphase eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without galvanic corrosion effects can distinguish the proposed explanation.
Total degradation, corrosion rate, wear rate, and microstructure are the response variables for the proposed comparison.
Similar total degradation in specimens with and without galvanic effects would falsify the hypothesis.
Lower total degradation in the specimen without galvanic effects would falsify the hypothesis.
The magnitude of accelerated degradation and the relative contributions of wear and corrosion are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says galvanic effects should increase total degradation, so lower degradation in the specimen without galvanic effects is the expected supporting result, not a falsifying result. Only equivalence or reversal, under a defined equivalence threshold, would challenge the prediction.
